Research

Two papers on how people and AI systems work together.

Behavioural & Social SciencesIRIS National Fair submission

Predicting AI-Reliance Miscalibration in Student–AI Interaction from Pre-Response Signals

Students often accept a wrong AI answer or reject a right one. I asked whether that can be predicted before the AI responds. I designed and ran a study with 168 students in Grades 7–9 under a full ethics review, then built and validated prediction models on the results.

168students, Grades 7–9
2,264AI-assisted attempts
0.552Macro-F1
Majority-class baseline
0.207
Difficulty-only rule
0.507
Random Forest model
0.552

Macro-F1 under five-fold student-grouped nested cross-validation. Problem difficulty was the strongest signal and confidence added a little. Findings are predictive, not causal, and the paper reports its limits openly.

Literature review

Do Expert Personas in Large Language Models Improve Factual Reliability?

A review of the evidence on whether telling a language model to act as an expert makes its answers more accurate, and what that means for people who rely on those answers.

Projects

Two live tools I built to teach and measure reasoning. Both are open to try.

NLP · Live demo

Reasoning Evaluator (ScienceBridge AI)

Paste a student’s argument and the Argument Intelligence Analyzer scores the quality of its reasoning, looking at logical structure, depth, evidence and clarity.

  • Model: transformer-based NLP, trained on 45K+ argument-quality samples
  • Result: 0.15 RMSE on evaluation
  • Hosted on: Hugging Face Spaces
Try the evaluator →
Education · Live platform

Logical: 3D Knowledge Continuum

A gamified critical-thinking platform where students move through 15 interactive 3D stages, from observation and basic logic to pattern intelligence and analytical thinking, earning XP and unlocking artifacts as they go.

  • Built for: school students in ScienceTech Foothold sessions
  • Structure: 15 staged nodes with XP, credits and a progress tracker
